messages:
ethan: Heads up — seeing a regression on the decode hotpath when paged + flash-v2 are enabled. 99th latency on small-batch (B=1-4) jumped from ~80ms -> ~240ms on Dedicated. Repro harness attached in the repo under infra/bench/decode_micro. Suspect KV-page boundary crosses causing extra kernel launches and kernel-selector flip mid-inference.

ethan: Quick paste of a profiling snippet from a single B=1 decode token (timings are per-token):
```
Kernel flash_v2_fused             time=0.92ms   launches=1
Kernel attention_paged_split      time=3.40ms   launches=4
KV page memcpy                    time=7.10ms   (page-cross)
Total (decode token)              time=11.42ms
```

jia: Hmm. Do we have the kernel-selector logs for that run? Might be the continuous-batcher heuristic misclassifying first step as prefill and then switching to decode kernel which forces an internal flush.

ethan: Yep, pasted relevant logs: 
`[kernel-selector] seq_len=8, batch_sz=1 -> prefer=flash_prefill_variant; later step-> prefer=flash_decode_fused; action=hot-swap`
That hot-swap shows up as two kernel launches for what used to be one.

sam: We've flagged similar effects during prior tuning of flash_v2 — it helps large contiguous attention but the state machine for paged KV can cause extra copies when page index changes. We should check distribution of KV page IDs across tokens. If pages are scattered, page fusion loses its benefit.

maya: Another angle: if KV eviction/pinning happens (e.g., heavy multi-tenant churn), memcpy cost dominates tiny decode batches. Try warm cache vs cold cache runs. Also increase kv_page_size to see if fewer cross-page hits reduce jumps.

ethan: Repro commands I used:
```bash
./bench_decode --model=rw-medium-8k --mode=decode --batch=1 --iters=1000 --paged-kv=true --use-flash-v2=true
# trace output -> infra/traces/decode_kv_skew/2054128471.trace
```
Observed aggregated numbers (1000 iters): throughput 82 tok/s, p50 35ms, p95 120ms, p99 240ms. With flash-v1 (fallback) throughput 110 tok/s, p99 90ms.

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: build=2025-03-12-rc3 model=rw-medium-8k path=decode p99+150% vs baseline. Creating tag eng-runtime/perf/regress/2054128471 and pinging oncall.

jia: Can you capture cublas/cupti timeline for a short run (10 iters) and drop it into /tmp and link here? Need to confirm whether extra kernel launches are GPU-side or from CPU orchestration.

ethan: Will upload a 10-iter cucapture later today. I also have a microprofile showing the continuous_batcher flushing queues when page mismatch occurs. Excerpt: `continuous_batcher: flush_reason=kernel_switch, flushed_ngroup=1`

sam: I'll take ownership of the bench matrix: toggles = {flash_v2_on/off, paged_kv_on/off, kernel_selector_thresholds=[0.1,0.5,1.0], kv_page_size=[64,128,256]} and run across 3 Dedicated shapes today. Will post raw CSVs.

maya: I'll try the warm/cold cache runs and a config where we bias the selector to prefer decode kernel for B<=4 (temporary). If that helps, we can add a fallback heuristic until we solve page fusion logic.

ethan: Plan summary: 1) reproduce + cucapture (ethan) 2) bench matrix (sam) 3) warm/cold page experiments + selector bias (maya) 4) add micro-batching trace metric to console dashboard (jia). If anyone sees a quick mitigation, please post a small toggle we can ship to Dedicated as an opt-in.

sam: I'll post initial CSVs by EOD. If helpful, I can also try disabling page fusion entirely to measure worst-case memcpy cost.

maya: Also flagging this for the RTA board — if decode p99 stays high many customers will notice. :warning:

ethan: Thanks — appreciate quick eyes. I'll update the thread with cucapture and a minimal repro gist.
